sources.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems
sources.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 1–2, complete model setup and weak-space discussion.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 34-page PDF and read §1.1 in full. It formulates Y(g) for every g in the observation Hilbert space, gives the isonormal covariance, notes that sample paths need not be continuous linear functionals on H, and describes a negative Hilbert-scale realization. This supports the functional sample-space convention and does not assert an H-valued observation.

contents.name: Linear-Gaussian set-up and functional observation model
contents.support: Supports the family of indexed functionals, covariance convention, and distinction between a functional sample and an observation-space vector.

contents.name: Negative Hilbert-scale sample-space interpretation
contents.support: Supports the warning that white noise has a distributional carrier and is not generally an H-valued sample; the local theorem proves its own coordinate and mean-square claims.

sources.title: Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models
sources.locator: §1.2.2, equations (1.6)–(1.8), PDF pp. 21–22; isonormal construction from Brownian increments, PDF pp. 483–484.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 705-page book PDF and read the full relevant passages. §1.2.2 defines the white-noise observation as all indexed Gaussian functionals, identifies independent standard-normal coordinates in an orthonormal basis, states that the full sequence is not in l2, and explains the coordinate experiment. The later construction defines the isonormal process by L2 limits of simple functions. This is the independent book treatment for the A page.

contents.name: Gaussian white-noise functionals and sequence coordinates
contents.support: Supports the Hilbert-indexed process, independent basis coordinates, sequence sample space, and non-l2 qualification. The local proof establishes the exact mean-square reconstruction.

contents.name: Functional experiment definition
contents.support: Provides an independent full-text treatment of the isonormal functional observation model.

contents.name: Isonormal process construction from Brownian increments
contents.support: Constructs the L2-indexed process by completing simple-function stochastic integrals and identifies its isometry property.

contents.name: Finite coordinate example
contents.locator: §1.2.2, Gaussian sequence model equation (1.8), PDF pp. 21–22
contents.support: Provides the finite orthonormal-coordinate observation convention used in the example.

contents.name: Infinite coefficient sequence and finite truncation context
contents.support: Gives the Gaussian sequence model and its product coordinate laws.

contents.name: Finite basis projection context
contents.support: Supports the coordinate projection setting; the local example derives the omitted tail exactly.

sources.title: Ismaël Castillo and Richard Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise
sources.locator: §1.2, Definition 2 and equations (7)–(8), printed pp. 2004–2006 (PDF pp. 5–6); §3 coordinate representation, PDF pp. 13–14.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 30-page PDF and read the full relevant definition and coordinate passages. The source defines the negative Sobolev coefficient space and its log weights, states the white-noise basis-coordinate model, and gives the scale condition used for a Borel white-noise carrier.

contents.name: Negative Sobolev coefficient space for white noise
contents.support: Supports the H(delta) carrier and its scale condition; the local theorem cites the existing proved carrier lemma for its Borel-law conclusion.

contents.name: White-noise coordinate representation
contents.support: Provides an independent coefficient-sequence description and independent standard-normal coordinates.

contents.name: Finite truncation and coefficient tail
contents.support: Provides the finite orthogonal-coordinate setting; the local verification computes the omitted functional tail.

sources.title: Litao Ding and Peter Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions
sources.locator: §1, equations (1)–(3), PDF pp. 11–12. The source design's §2 locator is noted in the batch notes; §2 begins the minimax theorem proof.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete seven-page PDF and read §1 equations (1)–(3) in full. The source assumes a compact linear operator between Hilbert spaces and gives the SVD sequence model under the stated kernel-orthogonality condition. These operator-specific assumptions are not imported into the local white-noise representation theorem.

contents.name: Statistical inverse model and SVD sequence representation
contents.support: Provides context for the Gaussian inverse sequence model under compact-operator SVD assumptions; the local theorem proves the basis representation without requiring compactness or an SVD.
